fullPassage:
Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students.

This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs, including social, educational, and counseling services.

Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for spending time with the elderly residents. Many students were struggling to afford the area's high rents, so the proposal was a true win-win situation. Now, let's hear more about this intriguing place from two of the residents.

Hi! My name is Jacob Jansen, and I've been living at Humanitas for over two years. I've really enjoyed my time here. As a live-in student, I'm required to spend at least 30 hours per month with my elderly neighbors in exchange for free accommodations. In reality, however, we spend a lot more time together than that. Sometimes I teach them things, such as how to use social media, and other times I just hang out with them. We have meals together, play games, and go shopping.

Humanitas doesn't feel like a care home to me. Instead, I consider it a community that I am a part of. Every time I come home, I tell my neighbors about my day. When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. With so much experience gathered over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to acquire. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without realizing it. For example, I've learned the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee from them. It's a really great way to take a break from rushing around all the time.

I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I focused only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do. Obviously, Humanitas provides me with much more than a free place to stay. I've made deep, meaningful friendships that I'll never forget here.

I intend to stay at Humanitas for at least one more year. Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really grateful for this transformative experience. I have learned so much from my neighbors already, but I'm sure there is still a lot more that they can teach me.

My name is Helena Smit, and I am 93 years old. I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors. Believe me, not everyone was happy about it! But that quickly changed once they moved in. The students here are energetic, friendly, and caring. They make us laugh and create a joyful mood.

Humanitas was already a decent place to live before the students arrived, but it has become a lot more fun since they moved in. Recently, the students held a pajama party and invited us to join them. They taught us how to play some new games, and we all had a great time. It was like we were in our 20s again.

I sometimes hear loud music from my young next-door neighbor's apartment, but that is okay. It's a small matter compared to what they've brought to our lives. I'm grateful every day that they have become part of our community.

Speaking of my young neighbor, she has been here for more than two years now. Last year, she went through a difficult time of grief after she lost her father, so I did what came naturally. I stayed with her, held her hands when she cried, and listened to what she said. She later told me that I was a great comfort during that difficult time, which made me feel very good. It always feels nice to be reminded that I'm still capable of doing things for others.

I am nearly 100 years old, and I have bad knees. I understand that my knees aren't going to get any better. There is nothing much the doctors can do about the pain. But having young, vibrant people around helps me forget about the pain and enjoy my life!

There are currently six students living at Humanitas, with a long waiting list of others hoping to be offered a spot. Humanitas is a great example of how people of different ages can help each other and share their lives with one another. The older residents gain a more youthful perspective on life, while the younger residents receive valuable life lessons. More and more care homes around Europe are now trying intergenerational living, bringing the young and old together in harmony.

questions.passage: Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require (A)[assistance / resistance]. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students. This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the loss of many (B)[essential / optional] elderly care programs, including social, educational, and counseling services. Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for spending time with the elderly residents. Many students were struggling to (C)[afford / neglect] the area's high rents, so the proposal was a true win-win situation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 도움(assistance)이 필요한 노인, 필수적인(essential) 프로그램, 높은 임대료를 감당하다(afford).
det.analysis:
✅ ① assistance — essential — afford ←정답
(A) assistance(도움) — 노인이 '도움'이 필요한 요양 센터.
(B) essential(필수적인) — 예산 삭감으로 '필수' 프로그램 상실.
(C) afford(감당하다) — 학생들이 높은 임대료를 '감당하기' 어려움.

❌ ② resistance(저항) — 문맥에 맞지 않음.
❌ ③ optional(선택적인) — essential과 반의어.
❌ ④ resistance + optional — 둘 다 부적절.
det.tip: assistance = 도움, 원조. essential = 필수적인. afford = 감당하다, 여유가 있다.

When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. With so much experience (A)[gathered / scattered] over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to (B)[acquire / discard]. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without realizing it. For example, I've learned the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee from them. It's a really great way to take a break from rushing around all the time. I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I focused only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do. Obviously, Humanitas provides me with much more than a free place to stay. I've made deep, (C)[meaningful / trivial] friendships that I'll never forget here.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 평생에 걸쳐 모은(gathered) 경험, 아직 습득하지(acquire) 못한 지식, 깊고 의미 있는(meaningful) 우정.
det.analysis:
❌ ① scattered(흩어진) — 경험은 모으는 것. 반의어.

✅ ② gathered — acquire — meaningful ←정답
(A) gathered(모은) — '평생에 걸쳐 모은 경험'.
(B) acquire(습득하다) — '아직 습득하지 못한 지식'.
(C) meaningful(의미 있는) — '깊고 의미 있는 우정'.

❌ ③ discard(버리다) + trivial(하찮은) — 둘 다 반의어.
❌ ④ scattered + discard — 둘 다 부적절.
det.tip: gathered(모은) ↔ scattered(흩어진). acquire(습득하다) ↔ discard(버리다). meaningful(의미 있는) ↔ trivial(하찮은).

I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors. Believe me, not everyone was happy about it! questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 활기찬(energetic) 학생들, 아버지를 잃은 슬픔(grief)의 시간, Helena가 큰 위안(comfort)이 되었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① lethargic(무기력한) — '웃게 만들고 즐거운 분위기'와 모순.

❌ ② relief(안도) — 아버지를 '잃은' 뒤이므로 안도가 아니라 슬픔.

✅ ③ energetic — grief — comfort ←정답
(A) energetic(활기찬) — 학생들이 활기차고 친절하며 돌봐줌.
(B) grief(슬픔) — 아버지를 잃은 어려운 슬픔의 시간.
(C) comfort(위안) — Helena가 그 어려운 시기에 큰 위안.

❌ ④ burden(짐) — 'feel very good'과 모순. 짐이 아니라 위안.
det.tip: energetic(활기찬) ↔ lethargic(무기력한). grief(슬픔) ↔ relief(안도). comfort(위안) ↔ burden(짐).

det.analysis:
✅ ① supportive(지원하는): 원문 그대로. 요양 센터의 지원 환경.

❌ ② expansion(확대) → reduction(삭감): 예산 삭감(budget cuts) 결과로 자금이 '줄어든' 것. '확대'는 모순. ←정답

✅ ③ numerous(다수의): 원문 그대로. 빈 방이 여러 개 있었다.

✅ ④ win-win(상호 이익): 원문 그대로. 학생과 노인 모두에게 이익.
det.tip: reduction(감소, 삭감) ↔ expansion(확대, 증가). budget cuts → funding reduction이 자연스러움.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 energetic과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: energetic(활기찬) ↔ sluggish(느릿한, 활기 없는)
det.analysis:
❌ ① cheerful(쾌활한): energetic과 유사한 긍정적 의미.

❌ ② active(활동적인): energetic과 동의어.

❌ ③ lively(생기 있는): energetic과 동의어.

✅ ④ sluggish(느릿한) ←정답
→ energetic(활기찬) ↔ sluggish(느릿한, 무기력한).
det.tip: energetic = active = lively = 활기찬. ↔ sluggish = lethargic = 느릿한, 무기력한.

questions.passage:
I am nearly 100 years old, and I have bad knees. I understand that my knees aren't going to get any better. There is nothing much the doctors can do about the pain. But having young, <u>vibrant</u> people around helps me forget about the pain and enjoy my life!

There are currently six students living at Humanitas, with a long waiting list of others hoping to be offered a spot.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 vibrant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: vibrant(활기 넘치는) ↔ dull(활기 없는, 둔한)
det.analysis:
✅ ① dull(활기 없는) ←정답
→ vibrant(활기 넘치는, 생기 있는) ↔ dull(활기 없는, 칙칙한).

❌ ② dynamic(역동적인): vibrant와 유사.

❌ ③ spirited(활발한): vibrant와 동의어.

❌ ④ vigorous(정력적인): vibrant와 유사.
det.tip: vibrant = lively = dynamic = 활기 넘치는. ↔ dull = lifeless = 활기 없는.

questions.passage:
(A) It is a care center that <u>houses</u> more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual.

(B) Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations. The old <u>houses</u> in the neighborhood were being renovated as well.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 houses가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A)의 houses는 동사 '수용하다', (B)의 houses는 명사 '주택들'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 수용하다 — 건물들: (B)는 '건물'이 아닌 '주택'.

❌ ② 건물들 — 수용하다: (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜.

✅ ③ 수용하다 — 주택들 ←정답
(A) houses = 동사. '160명 이상의 노인을 수용한다'. care center가 주어이므로 '수용하다'.
(B) houses = 명사 복수형. '오래된 주택들'. 문맥상 건물로서의 집.

❌ ④ 주택들 — 건물들: (A)는 명사가 아닌 동사.
det.tip: house: (동사) 수용하다, 거처를 제공하다 / (명사) 집, 주택. 문장에서 품사 구분이 핵심.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "involving or relating to people of different age groups"

det.korean: '서로 다른 연령대의 사람들을 포함하거나 관련된' = intergenerational(세대 간의)
det.analysis:
❌ ① international(국제적인): 국가 간 관계.

❌ ② interpersonal(대인 관계의): 사람 간 관계이지만 연령 구분 없음.

✅ ③ intergenerational(세대 간의) ←정답
→ inter(~사이의) + generational(세대의) = 서로 다른 세대 간의.

❌ ④ interdisciplinary(학제 간의): 학문 분야 간 관계.
det.tip: inter- = ~사이의. intergenerational = 세대 간의. 본문의 'intergenerational living' = 세대 간 공동 생활.

questions.passage: Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really grateful for this __________ (transform) experience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: transform(변형하다) → transformative(변화를 가져다주는). 명사 experience를 수식하는 형용사 필요.
det.analysis:
원문: 'I'm really grateful for this transformative experience.'
→ 빈칸 뒤 명사 experience를 수식하는 형용사가 필요.
→ transform(동사) → transformative(형용사): 변화를 가져다주는.

변형 과정: transform + -ative = transformative
det.tip: transform(v.) → transformation(n.) → transformative(adj.). -ative = '~하는 성질의' 형용사 접미사.

questions.passage: It always feels nice to be reminded that I'm still __________ (capability) of doing things for others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: capability(능력) → capable(능력 있는). be capable of ~ing = ~할 수 있는.
det.analysis:
원문: 'I'm still capable of doing things for others.'
→ be __________ of ~ing 구조에서 형용사 capable 필요.
→ capability(명사) → capable(형용사).

변형 과정: capability(n.) → capable(adj.)
det.tip: capable(adj.) = ~할 수 있는. capability(n.) = 능력. be capable of ~ing = ~할 능력이 있다.

questions.passage:
Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students.

This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to __________.

overlay.blank: the loss of many essential elderly care programs

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the loss of many essential elderly care programs

det.korean: 자금 삭감의 결과로 많은 필수 노인 돌봄 프로그램의 상실(the loss of many essential elderly care programs)로 이어졌다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the construction of new buildings
(새 건물 건설)
→ 자금 삭감 결과가 건설은 모순.

❌ ② an increase in student enrollment
(학생 등록 증가)
→ 학생 입주는 해결책이지 삭감의 직접 결과가 아님.

❌ ③ the expansion of medical facilities
(의료 시설 확장)
→ 자금 삭감 → 확장은 논리적 모순.

✅ ④ the loss of many essential elderly care programs ←정답
(많은 필수 노인 돌봄 프로그램 상실)
→ 원문: 'led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs'.
det.tip: lead to = ~로 이어지다. funding reduction(자금 삭감) → loss(상실)가 인과 관계.

questions.passage:
Humanitas doesn't feel like a care home to me. Instead, I consider it a community that I am a part of. Every time I come home, I tell my neighbors about my day. When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. With so much experience gathered over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to acquire. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without realizing it. For example, I've learned the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee from them. It's a really great way to __________.

I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I focused only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do.

overlay.blank: take a break from rushing around all the time

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: take a break from rushing around

det.korean: 커피 한 잔을 마시며 편하게 대화하는 것의 가치 → 바쁘게 돌아다니는 것에서 쉬는(take a break from rushing around) 방법.
det.analysis:
✅ ① take a break from rushing around ←정답
(바쁘게 돌아다니는 것에서 쉬다)
→ 원문: 'take a break from rushing around all the time'. 커피 대화 = 바쁜 일상에서 벗어나 쉬는 방법.

❌ ② build professional connections
(전문적 인맥을 쌓다)
→ 전문적 관계가 아닌 여유로운 대화의 맥락.

❌ ③ improve academic grades quickly
(학업 성적을 빠르게 올리다)
→ 편안한 대화와 학업 성적은 무관.

❌ ④ learn advanced cooking skills
(고급 요리 기술을 배우다)
→ 요리와 무관한 맥락.
det.tip: take a break from ~ = ~에서 벗어나 쉬다. casual chat(편한 대화) = 바쁜 일상의 여유.
